raw:
I haven't checked these against the benchmark data; they come from reasoning about how Adam-trained ReLU MLPs behave over 243 epochs.

- **Learning rate:** very high values (0.0774 to 1) tend to diverge, so raising the rate there should hurt. Very low values (1e-5 to 1.3e-4) leave the model under-trained, so raising the rate there should help.
- **Batch size:** a larger batch means fewer updates per epoch. That hurts when the learning rate is low and helps when it is high, where the noise reduction stabilizes training. Very small batches (4 to 10) are noisy, so going up from them should help.
- **Alpha:** an L2 penalty in the top band (0.129 to 1) over-regularizes, so raising it further should hurt.
- **Depth and width:** extra depth or width adds instability at a high learning rate. When capacity is already small, extra width or depth should help.
